subject: Re: Post-call: caching assumptions & target $/1M tokens
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - caching assumptions / target $/1M tokens

Thanks again for a great call this morning, Emma - really appreciate the openness on volumes and priorities. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can align on pricing:

Summary (what we heard)
- FastRetail usage profile: ~12-18M tokens/month expected in the first 6 months as you roll the feature out to power product search + short-form personalization.
- Prompt shape: Short user prompts (~20-60 tokens) + longer context (100-800 tokens) for product metadata in many calls.
- Priority: get within your target budget band while preserving quality (no hallucination trade-offs).

Pricing discussion items / assumptions we used on the call
- Baseline (no caching) unit compute cost we model for your profile: $1,200 per 1M tokens served.
- Caching levers: prefix/KV cache for repeated product context and prompt prefixes.
- Cache hit rate assumption we used on the whiteboard: 40%-60% depending on how much of the 100-800 token context is repeatable across requests.

What we need from you to finalize a proposal
1) Confirm a realistic monthly volume range to price against (you mentioned ~15M as a mid-point).
2) Approx share of calls that are identical/near-identical prompts (search templates, system prompt) vs. unique end-user text.
3) Any firm budget targets (e.g., target effective $/1M tokens or monthly spend cap).

What we attached
- RWD-pricing-model-v2.xlsx - editable model that lets you toggle cache hit rate, percent of context cached, and see effective $/1M tokens + monthly spend.
- example-prompt-sample.json - small sample of the prompt shapes you described (so our infra team can run a quick cache-hit simulation).

Next steps
- If you can confirm the three items above this week, Marcus and I will run the model with 3 hit-rate scenarios (conservative/expected/optimistic) and send back a 1-page pricing summary + recommended pilot (2-week run to validate hit rate with traffic).

Thanks - talk soon.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Ross <emma@fastretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap & next steps - caching assumptions / target $/1M tokens

Thanks Emma - quick pass with the math and the caching assumptions we recommend. I plugged your mid-point (15M/mo) into the attached model and ran three hit-rate scenarios. High-level: caching mainly reduces the number of "served" tokens (what you pay per token) by returning cached prefix results locally; the more of the 100-800 token context that is repeatable, the bigger the hit rate.

Assumptions used
- Baseline (no cache): model/compute + infra blended cost = $1,200 per 1M tokens served. (This is the number Marissa referenced; it's our internal blended cost used for sales math - see workbook.)
- Cache semantics: prefix cache for repeated product metadata + system prompts. When a request hits cache we do not re-run the full forward compute for the cached prefix; only the delta tokens are served to the model.
- Effective served tokens = (1 - hit_rate) * total_tokens_served_by_model. For example, a 50% effective hit rate across the full context means you run full compute for roughly half the tokens.

Numbers (per 1M raw tokens of incoming request traffic)
- No caching: effective cost = $1,200 / 1M tokens.
- 30% hit rate: effective tokens served = 70% -> effective cost ~ $840 / 1M tokens. (1,200 * 0.7)
- 50% hit rate: effective cost ~ $600 / 1M tokens.
- 70% hit rate: effective cost ~ $360 / 1M tokens.

Applied to your volume (15M/mo) -> monthly spend bands (approx):
- No cache: 15 * $1,200 = $18,000/mo
- 30% hit: 15 * $840 = $12,600/mo
- 50% hit: 15 * $600 = $9,000/mo
- 70% hit: 15 * $360 = $5,400/mo

Notes / caveats
- These numbers assume the cache hit rate percent applies across the full token envelope (prefix + context). In practice you'll see a higher hit rate on short, repeated prefixes (system prompt, product snippet) and lower on free-text user content. The workbook breaks down context vs. prompt-level hits so you can tune the inputs.
- Cache warm-up & cold-start: initial pilot weeks will show lower hit rates until popular prefixes are warm; recommend a 2-week pilot with production traffic and logging to measure realistic hit rates.
- Prefix size & TTL: larger prefix caching (caching 200-400 tokens of context) increases hit compression but also increases memory pressure and eviction churn; we'll propose a conservative default (cache top 200 tokens per item) for the pilot.

Recommendation / next step
1) Run the 2-week pilot using your sample traffic (we'll provide a small SDK wrapper and the logging config).
2) We'll produce a post-pilot report with observed hit rates + final effective $/1M and recommended caching profile.

I can also run a quick sensitivity table for other budget targets if you want to share the exact target $/1M.

--Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
